correctness.rationale: Discrete-gradient identity proves the half-line spectral edge at v=1/2; geometric eigenvector plus rank-one Weyl theory prove the support and boundary attainment classification. Exact Chebyshev determinant and positive n,n-1,...,1 eigenvector prove finite crossing. Monotonicity of k cot k and kappa coth kappa gives the two-sided Robin limit; fixed-t sinusoidal/hyperbolic analysis gives sharp convergence, and t_n cos(beta/sqrt n) shifts alpha to alpha-beta^2/4. The replayable checker validates 261 finite assertions; infinite conclusions are analytic.

value.rationale: An intrinsically motivated finite-section question for a natural rank-one-defected unilateral shift is completely solved, with a full ordinary-vs-essential range distinction, exact finite crossing, universal two-parameter angular/radial Robin boundary layer, and sharp fixed-coupling rates. The result classifies geometry and spectral approximation rather than giving an arbitrary numerical slice; its scope is exactly the single diagonal boundary defect.
